bull.b: A domestic refinery focused on battery-grade lithium gives Stardust Power exposure to the strategic buildout of U.S. battery materials capacity. If execution succeeds, the planned business could serve growing EV and energy-storage manufacturing demand while supporting a more localized supply chain.

bull.t: Low Reported Debt Relative To Assets
bull.b: Reported debt remains low relative to the asset base, limiting the direct burden of interest and scheduled debt repayment. This provides some financial flexibility compared with a highly leveraged developer, although the benefit is constrained by negative equity and continuing operating cash outflows.

bull.t: Recent Improvement From Prior Loss And Cash-flow Levels
bull.b: The narrowing of losses from 2024 indicates some improvement in reported earnings performance, while the cash-flow summary also notes better free cash flow than in 2025. Continued progress could eventually reduce funding pressure, though the company has not yet reached positive earnings or cash generation.

bear.b: Stardust Power has not demonstrated commercial revenue from its planned lithium business, yet it continues to incur substantial losses. The absence of a revenue base makes future margins and profitability unproven, increasing execution risk as the company develops its refinery plans.

bear.t: Negative Equity And Persistent Cash Burn
bear.b: Negative equity reflects accumulated deficits and leaves the company with a thin capital cushion, while ongoing operating and free-cash-flow losses consume funding. This combination can constrain development spending and increase reliance on external capital to sustain operations and execute its strategy.

The Nasdaq suspension and delisting decision can reduce market access and liquidity, while the company’s expanded equity issuance capacity and default-related note conversion show continued dependence on capital markets. Further financing may dilute holders or address obligations without solving the underlying operating deficit.
